yt_description:
The whole village laughed when Sam built ten birdhouses for zero birds… until harvest. 🦉🌾
Barn owls hunt rodents all night: a pair with its chicks can catch 2,000–6,000 rodents a year. Israeli farmers put up their first 14 owl nest boxes in 1983 (Kibbutz Sde Eliyahu); today there are thousands, and much less rat poison is used. (Sam is a fictional character; the owls are real science.)

Sources: Frontiers for Young Minds (2023) "Israel's Barn Owl Project"; Ardea (2009) nest-box study, Beit She'an Valley.

script: This farmer spends his money on wooden boxes for birds. And the whole village thinks he has lost his mind. Mice are eating his wheat. Every night, hundreds of them chew through the field. His neighbor buys traps, cats, and buckets of poison. Nothing works. But old Sam hammers together a wooden box, and nails it on top of a tall pole. The village laughs. A birdhouse? The mice are on the ground, Sam! Then Sam does something even stranger. He builds nine more. The village laughs even louder. Ten birdhouses for zero birds? Sam just smiles. And waits. One night, a pale heart-shaped face peeks out of the box. Then another. By harvest, his wheat stands tall and golden. His neighbor's field is full of holes. That night, the neighbor knocks on his door. Sam... can you build me a box? Those were barn owls. They hunt all night, and a pair with chicks can catch two thousand to six thousand rodents a year. Farmers in Israel put up their first fourteen owl boxes in 1983. Today there are thousands, and much less poison is used.
